host: Amp orb, 2 vCPU, 4 GB; vegeta, Postgres 15 and the server on the same CPUs

server.per_request: frankenphp php-server --root public (classic mode, no memory between requests, like PHP-FPM)

payload: bench/targets.php: 1,000 distinct ses-v2 SendEmail requests, ~24 KB MIME

kill_tests.method: vegeta 10 s at the given rate; after 5 s SIGKILL every server process and delete the buffer directory (a deploy or instance loss); systemd restarts the server with an empty tmp dir; compare 200-acknowledged MessageIds with sesame_messages
kill_tests.classification: Both losses whose MessageIds were captured were reported by IngestBuffer::lossFor() as status=lost, seq = drained_through + 1 of the replaced buffer. (The first five 300/s runs did not capture IDs.)
kill_tests.not_measured: Loss when the after-response drain does not run (Postgres down, process killed in the deferred callback): then only the scheduled per-second drain empties the buffer, so up to ~1 s of sends (about 30 at 30/s) plus whatever accumulated while Postgres was unreachable.
